text: Lesson 12 built a real failover group. But a mechanism that's configured and a mechanism that's proven to work are two different things. A DR plan nobody has ever actually triggered is a plan on paper. This lesson tests it deliberately, before Chapter 7's unannounced drill does it under pressure.

Switch-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup triggers the test — and notice it's run against the secondary server's name, not the primary. You're telling the secondary to become the new primary, not telling the primary to step down.

The secondary stops accepting replicated changes, gets promoted to primary, and the listener endpoint repoints automatically to the new primary. That last step is the entire reason the failover group was worth building — the application doesn't need to be told anything.

A real pass measures actual downtime against the one-hour RTO target, actual data loss against the five-minute RPO target, confirms the application reconnected on its own, and confirms the data on the new primary is correct. Next lesson looks at what's actually happening underneath this — the geo-replication mechanism itself.
